# 金籙十迴度人午朝開收儀-明

**ID:** KR5b0187
**Custom ID:** ZB5b0187

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

Second of the *shíhuí dùrén kāishōu* triad ([KR5b0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0186), [KR5b0187](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0187), [KR5b0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0188)), transmitted under 三儀同卷軆九.

**Abstract**

The noon *kāishōu* handles *huí* 5–8 of the ten-fold recitation cycle, opening and closing each in turn. The *huí* are distributed across the day in a *4-4-2* pattern: 1–4 in the morning (cf. [KR5b0186](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0186)), 5–8 at noon, and 9–10 in the evening (cf. [KR5b0188](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0188)); the pattern itself encodes the cosmological priority of noon — at the *yáng* zenith of the day — as the central salvific moment of the rite. Each *huí* opens with a *kāijīng wén* 開經文 and closes with a *shōujīng wén* 收經文, framing the recitation proper (which takes place in the companion *zhuǎnjīng* rite, [KR5b0190](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b0190)).

Per Schipper & Verellen (*Taoist Canon* 2: 996–997, John Lagerwey), the framework is part of the Sòng-Yuán expansion of the *Jīnlù* with the *Dùrén jīng* as its centrepiece; the textual transmission through the Míng *Zhèngtǒng dàozàng* (1444) places the *terminus ante quem* of canonisation while the *terminus a quo* is bounded by the Sòng codification of the *shíhuí* schema.
